prize_parts.citation: For the development of visible-light photoredox catalysis as a general tool for organic synthesis

statement.case_for: Visible-light photoredox catalysis made single-electron transfer from excited-state metal complexes and organic dyes a general, mild and predictable way to build bonds. The 2008-2009 reports opened radical pathways that thermal two-electron chemistry could not reach, and the field has since produced decarboxylative couplings, dual metal/photoredox catalysis and late-stage functionalization used routinely in pharmaceutical and materials laboratories. The mechanism is well characterized by quenching studies and spectroscopy, the technique is reproduced everywhere, and it is mature enough that the credit story has settled around three independent launch groups.
statement.case_against: Credit is crowded: Konig, Nicewicz, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi all have real claims, and a three-person cap forces painful omissions. MacMillan is already a 2021 laureate for organocatalysis, so a second prize to him invites a fair objection about repeat recognition and about the conceptual overlap with that prize. Some of the claimed synthetic advantages (mild conditions, scalability) are still debated, since photochemical scale-up and quantum-yield questions remain unresolved for many transformations.

responses.point: Nitrogenase is the central enzyme of biological N2 reduction; the structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor, including the interstitial carbide, are attributable mainly to Rees and Einsle, with Seefeldt supplying kinetic and mechanistic framework.
responses.response: I ranked nitrogenase fourth and take it seriously because the structural evidence is exactly what I look for: the central light atom was established by high-resolution crystallography and spectroscopy, not inferred. I agree Rees and Einsle carry the structural claim. I disagree that mechanism is as settled as the structure; how N2 binds and is reduced at the cofactor is still debated, so a citation must stay on structure and function of the cofactor rather than on a completed mechanism. Dean has a fair claim on the genetics and cofactor biosynthesis side, which Seefeldt does not replace. This is my best alternative, not my first choice, because the biological and inorganic framing fits a narrower audience than a general synthetic tool.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a new drug modality, with Crews and Deshaies conceiving PROTACs and Handa identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target, and clinical use maturing.
responses.response: The concept is real, and I moved it up in my own thinking, but I ranked it eighth for two reasons. First, I want structural proof of the ternary complexes, and the cooperativity picture rests on a limited number of crystal structures of degrader-bound E3/target assemblies, so the design rules are not yet generalized. Second, no PROTAC has been approved to my knowledge (not independently verified), so the claimed benefit to patients is still prospective. I also see the credit as split between two distinct achievements, PROTAC design and the thalidomide/cereblon mechanism, which a single three-person citation blurs. I would accept B044 as an alternative if the committee wants a medically driven prize, with Crews and Handa clearly in and Ciulli's structural contribution weighed against Deshaies.

responses.point: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade, with Miyasaka, Park and Snaith as the key originators and good conceptual value in defect tolerance.
responses.response: I put perovskites sixth and share the admiration for the efficiency trajectory, and I agree on Miyasaka, Park and Snaith as the credible trio, but I would hold back. Operational stability, lead toxicity and manufacturing at scale are unresolved, so the application story that makes the prize persuasive has not yet been shown outside the laboratory. It is also a materials-physics story where the chemistry of why the structure tolerates defects is still argued. The photoredox case has fewer outstanding technical caveats at the level of the chemistry itself. I would not object strongly if the committee chose it, and I would want Grätzel's dye-sensitized precedent acknowledged in the citation wording.

responses.point: Photoredox is a distinct, widely used toolbox, but MacMillan being a 2021 laureate complicates a fair configuration, and he ranks Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling first as a clean two-person case.
responses.response: You are right that MacMillan's earlier prize is the weakest point of my configuration, and I do not wave it away: the 2021 citation was for asymmetric organocatalysis, and the photoredox work is a separate mechanistic line, but it was in part developed in the same laboratory with overlapping style and trainees. If the committee judges a repeat unacceptable, I would revise to Yoon and Stephenson with Nicewicz or Konig, which is a weaker fit to the historical record. On Buchwald and Hartwig, the scientific case is strong and the attribution is cleaner than mine, but the transformation is now a mature reaction class and I did not rank it on my opening ballot; I would like to hear whether you see any reason it is still more novel than photoredox.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a second prize for MacMillan, or whether the configuration should drop him and credit Yoon, Stephenson and one of Nicewicz or Konig.
How to weigh Konig, Nicewicz, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi against the three-person cap without misrepresenting priority.
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism is mature enough, beyond the cofactor structure, to support a citation.
Whether degrader-bound ternary complex structures are now numerous enough to support general design rules for PROTACs.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, who ranks nitrogenase first, but that is a collegial connection rather than a collaboration or an institutional tie to any candidate, and my views on B032 were formed independently.
